subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec support inline PowerShell expansion tokens through explicit one-shot approval, or should OpenClaw document script-file use as the supported pattern?
rationale: Current code intentionally rejects expansion-looking tokens at the approval boundary, while the report asks for command-fidelity behavior that affects auto-review and reusable approval semantics.

options.title: Support One-Shot Expansion Approval
options.body: Adopt the active PR direction after native Windows/Gateway proof shows expansion commands reach explicit one-shot approval and complete without hanging.

options.title: Document Script-File Pattern
options.body: Keep rejecting inline PowerShell expansions and document `.ps1` files as the supported path for dollar-heavy PowerShell commands.

recommendation.title: Support One-Shot Expansion Approval
recommendation.body: Adopt the active PR direction after native Windows/Gateway proof shows expansion commands reach explicit one-shot approval and complete without hanging.

likelyOwner.reason: Jesse authored the current Windows command planner surface where the product/security contract needs to be decided.
